analyst_view.overall: Brighton are 2nd but lost 2-0 at Hull last time, with Costinha sent off; he is suspended here, and Mitoma, Ferguson, Tzimas and Yohanna are out, with Malick Yalcouye also injured. Fabian Hurzeler's side play Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League on Thursday night, three days before this, though he planned to rest some players there. Newcastle, 13th under Matthias Jaissle, drew 2-2 at Arsenal and have a free week; Joelinton and goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen are out, but club training footage shows Lewis Hall back with the squad after limping off at Arsenal. The numbers still treat Hall as out (about -6% on Newcastle's goals, +6% on Brighton's), and they count Simon Hooper's high card rate.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals: 1.9 for Brighton and 1.1 for Newcastle, and they treat Lewis Hall as out, which lifts Brighton by about 6% and lowers Newcastle by about 6%. Training footage reported on Thursday suggests Hall is fine (one report), so that boost to Brighton is probably too big; undoing it nets out at a small trim, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.8 corners, 5.2 for Brighton and 4.6 for Newcastle, already lowered a little because both have won fewer corners lately. Hall's return would add an overlapping left-back for Newcastle, but Brighton's possession game still drives their share, so nothing clearly moves and I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.4 cards, already including Simon Hooper's high rate (4.5 a game) and both teams being booked more than usual lately. Costinha's ban is already known and it is not a derby, so I stay at about 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 26.5 shots, 16.1 from Brighton, which already includes their heavy shooting lately. Brighton play in the Conference League on Thursday night, three days before, while Newcastle have a free week, and the numbers do not count that; Hurzeler is rotating some players, so I take only about 3% off, to about 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.6 shots on target, already lowered because both teams have hit the target less than expected lately. Brighton's short turnaround could cost a little sharpness, but they wasted good chances at Hull rather than failing to create them, so I stay at about 8.6.
